title: 1 HOUR AGO •Driver News Barcelona Is Ideal Spot for INDYCAR’s Latest International Event Reigning and five-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou of Chip Ganassi Racing (photo) is a Barcelona native.
excerpt:
The NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ return to Europe is more than a milestone on the calendar. It’s an opportunity for the series introduce its brand of high-speed, ultra-competitive racing to a new audience at one of the continent’s most recognizable motorsports venues.

The inaugural INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona is scheduled for Sunday, July 18 at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Spain. The event was the centerpiece of Phase Two of the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule. The multiyear agreement brings North America’s premier open-wheel racing series outside the continent for the first time since 2013, when James Hinchcliffe won on the streets of São Paulo. It also marks INDYCAR’s first European race since 2007 at TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands.

“We are called frequently by international tracks and potential partners, and everybody's reported that from time to time we'll talk to somebody and just see what's out there,” Penske Entertainment Corp. President and CEO Mark Miles said. “But then we got a call from Barcelona.”

The renowned road course that opened in 1991 has hosted Formula One and MotoGP events. Miles views this as an opportunity that could offer an established motorsports setting that will showcase the NTT INDYCAR SERIES while providing a strong foundation for a successful long-term partnership.

“This is an iconic track,” Miles said. “It’s the highest-level, highest-quality track, and we really got to know quickly the personnel, the executive staff, the governmental entities that look over the ownership of the track and believe these were people we could do business with. So, it just seemed like it's been four-ish months of work and discussions, but we felt like we could get here. And once we can be here, we think this is going to be a great home for the INDYCAR SERIES for many years to come.”

The announcement also carries a significance for Alex Palou that extends well beyond the championship implications of another race weekend. The 29-year-old Barcelona native captured his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship in 2026, becoming just the second driver in series history to win four consecutive titles, joining Sébastien Bourdais, who accomplished the feat from 2004-07. With five championships in six years and 25 career victories, Palou is tied for 17th on the series’ all-time wins list. Only A.J. Foyt, with seven titles, and Scott Dixon, with six, have won more championships. He now will compete in front of his home fans in an INDYCAR SERIES race that once seemed unimaginable.

“Incredible for me,” Palou said. “I never thought that there would be any day that INDYCAR would come to Barcelona. I dreamed about having the series go overseas and kind of going to Europe but never in my times and in Barcelona.

“It’s just a start, but I feel like everybody's super excited here. It's not like we're going to a place where they're not excited about INDYCAR or it's just another event for them. It will be the event next year here. Everybody's super pumped.

“I cannot thank the INDYCAR team enough for making this happen, the Barcelona team for making this happen. I'm just like a passenger here, and I'm just going to enjoy every single moment.”

Palou, who is the only Spaniard in the INDYCAR SERIES field, doesn’t believe he has to carry the burden of lifting an entire series through a country. He explained there are plenty of European drivers competing in the series, and Barcelona could provide an accessible destination for fans who have followed those drivers from afar but have never had the opportunity to see the series race on their home continent.

“It’ll be my hometown race, but it'll be the home race for more than 10 drivers that are from Europe, and they are only a couple hours away from here,” Palou said. “Hopefully, we get a lot of fans. We get a lot of new fans that they then get following all our schedule.”

The July race isn’t a one-year opportunity. The 2027 race weekend is the start of what both sides view as a potentially decade-long partnership, Miles said.

“This could be the home base for INDYCAR in Europe,” Miles said. “I think we're landing in the right place.”

title: IndyCar adding Barcelona, dropping Nashville; D.C. reportedly out, too
excerpt:
Five-time series champion Alex Palou will get a hometown race next year when IndyCar stages an event at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Spain.

It will mark IndyCar's first foray outside of North America since a 2013 race in Sao Paulo, Brazil. A North American-based open-wheel racing series last competed in Europe in 2007, when Champ Car put on an event in Assen, Netherlands.

In other changes to the IndyCar schedule for next year, an event will no longer be held in Nashville, and Motorsports.com reported that the Washington, D.C., race also will not return.

Palou captured his fourth straight IndyCar title this year, adding to his first championship in 2021. He is from Sant Antoni de Vilamajor, Spain, around an hour away from Barcelona. Palou has 25 victories in 116 career IndyCar races.

Salvador Illa, the president of the autonomous Spanish region of Catalonia, confirmed that he will attend a Friday event launching the local IndyCar race. Among the others expected to attend, according to Illa's office, is Mark Miles, the president and CEO of Penske Entertainment Corp., which owns the IndyCar Series.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya's 2.9-mile road track has hosted an annual Formula One race since 1991.

Nashville was the site of an IndyCar event on city streets each year from 2021-23, then at Nashville Superspeedway from 2024-26.

Scott Borchetta, chairman and CEO of Borchetta Bourbon, the title sponsor of the Nashville race, wrote in a statement on Thursday that he hopes the city can revive the event in the future.

"SMI and Nashville Superspeedway have been great partners in hosting the Borchetta Bourbon Music City Grand Prix for the last three years," Borchetta wrote. "But the original vision for the grand prix still stands -- to become 'The Monaco of the South.' If we don't put our complete focus and investment into returning downtown, it won't happen. IndyCar and FOX love Nashville, and there is a great desire to return to its downtown streets."

The D.C. event, the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, was created this year to coincide with celebrations for the United States' 250th anniversary. The race was held on a 1.7-mile street circuit around the National Mall.

This article first appeared on Field Level Media and was syndicated with permission.

title: 3 DAYS AGO •Exclusive News Phase Two of 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Schedule Unveiled
excerpt:
New Marquee Race Weekend in Barcelona Highlights Action-Packed Summer, Furthers Series Momentum

All NTT INDYCAR SERIES Races Again To Air on FOX

Following the historic announcement of an NTT INDYCAR SERIES race at iconic Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya earlier today, INDYCAR has announced Phase Two of next year’s action-packed and momentous schedule.

The summer lineup includes a mix of fan-friendly and dynamic race weekends leading up to the climactic moment at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca when the 2027 INDYCAR SERIES champion hoists the Astor Challenge Cup.

For the third consecutive season, all races will be broadcast on FOX in the United States, with three additional telecasts scheduled during the two days of qualifying for the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge and coverage of Miller Lite Carb Day at Indianapolis Motor Speedway. The NTT INDYCAR SERIES is once again the only premier motorsports series in North America with all races broadcast on network television.

“The 2027 season will build off a record-shattering and landmark year for the NTT INDYCAR SERIES,” Penske Entertainment Corp. President and CEO Mark Miles said. “The sport’s growth has been immense, driving incredible viewership gains, reaching new fans in younger demos and attracting increased commercial interest from emerging and long-term partners. Our relationship with FOX Sports continues to set an industry standard, and this schedule will help us build on all of these gains and take things to the next level.”

After announcing Phase One of the 2027 schedule in August, Phase Two of the 17-race championship picks up Sunday, June 13 at World Wide Technology Raceway near St. Louis. In 2026, the race on the challenging 1.25-mile oval featured 17 lead changes, wheel-to-wheel action throughout the field and an INDYCAR SERIES track-record 268 passes for position.

Two weeks later, the NTT INDYCAR SERIES heads to picturesque Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin, for the series’ 37th race at historic Road America on Sunday, June 27. Known for its sweeping corners, long straightaways and 4-mile layout, the historic road course remains one of the fastest and most demanding circuits on the schedule.

Racing at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course has become a Fourth of July holiday tradition for INDYCAR, and it will continue Sunday, July 4. The technical, 2.258-mile, 13-turn road course, known for its elevation changes and tight corners, will host its 44th INDYCAR SERIES race in 2027, the longest-running road course event on the schedule.

Following the international showcase in Barcelona, the series returns to the Pacific Northwest for its annual stop at Portland International Raceway on Sunday, Aug. 1. The 12-turn road course is known for its challenging opening chicane and history of thrilling finishes. In 2026, four different race teams were represented among the top four finishers.

The series then crosses the border into Canada for the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham on Sunday, Aug. 15, on the Streets of Markham. The 2.19-mile temporary street circuit, which debuted in 2026, features 12 turns, a double-sided pit lane and technically challenging sections. The 2026 race featured 258 on-track passes, the most of any street circuit last season.

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship enters its final stretch with a return to the historic Milwaukee Mile for a pivotal doubleheader Saturday and Sunday, Aug. 28-29. The legendary 1-mile oval, which opened in 1903, features relatively flat corners that demand precision and offers drivers two opportunities to earn valuable championship points in one weekend. Last year’s first 250-lap race featured a season-high 696 on-track passes and track records for passes for position, passes in the top 10 and passes in the top five.

The final round of the 2027 season is scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 5 at legendary WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca in Monterey, California. The iconic 2.238-mile road course features 11 turns, dramatic elevation changes and the world-famous Corkscrew turn complex, providing a fitting showcase for the final race of the 17-event championship and the presentation of the Astor Challenge Cup, manufacturer award and Rookie of the Year award. It is the 13th time the legendary circuit on the Central Coast will host the INDYCAR SERIES season finale.

“One of the things that makes INDYCAR so special is that winning a championship requires drivers and teams to be competitive on every type of racetrack,” INDYCAR President J. Douglas Boles said. “From high-speed ovals to tight street circuits and challenging road courses, they face a different test almost every weekend. The 2027 schedule continues that tradition, featuring the 111th Running of the Indianapolis 500, alongside some of the most iconic racetracks in North America, and the historic addition of Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya. With 25 full-time entries battling for a championship and every race broadcast on FOX, our fans have an incredible season of racing to look forward to.”

Tune-in times for next season’s events will be announced at a later date. The 2027 schedule for INDY NXT by Firestone, INDYCAR’s developmental series, also will be announced in the coming weeks.

title: 3 DAYS AGO •Driver News Marquee Event Coming to Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in 2027
excerpt:
North America’s Premier Open-Wheel Racing Series Makes Historic Debut at Home of Five-Time NTT INDYCAR SERIES Champion Alex Palou

INDYCAR is expanding its global footprint in historic fashion, announcing a marquee international event at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Spain as the centerpiece of Phase Two of the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule.

The inaugural INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona is scheduled for Sunday, July 18 and will bring North America’s premier open-wheel racing series to Spain for the first time, setting the stage for a spectacular homecoming for Barcelona native and five-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou of Chip Ganassi Racing.

The multiyear agreement with Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya marks the NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ first race outside North America since 2013, when James Hinchcliffe won on the streets of São Paulo, Brazil. The event also signals a European return for the INDYCAR SERIES, which last competed on the continent in 2007 at the TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands.

“This is a monumental day for our sport,” Penske Entertainment Corp. President and CEO Mark Miles said. “We are pleased to be able to take our ultra-competitive brand of wheel-to-wheel racing to Europe and thrilled that we can showcase INDYCAR in Alex Palou’s hometown. We have seen Alex’s remarkable skill and talent for several years and know his fans in Spain have been clamoring to watch him race in person.

“We cannot wait to see the NTT INDYCAR SERIES compete at one of the world’s most recognizable motorsports venues set against the backdrop of a very historic and breathtaking international destination like Barcelona.”

Palou, a 29-year-old Spaniard, captured his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship in 2026, becoming just the second driver in series history to win four consecutive titles, joining Sebastien Bourdais (2004-07). With five championships in six years and 25 career victories, Palou is tied for 17th on the series’ all-time wins list. Only A.J. Foyt (seven) and Scott Dixon (six) have won more INDYCAR SERIES championships.

“I’m so excited to be part of INDYCAR’s first race in Barcelona,” Palou said. “It is an amazing opportunity, and it means so much to me to have a race at home in Barcelona, it’s hard to put into words. I know the fans are going to love it, and I think we are going to put on a great show. We’re going to try hard with the team at Chip Ganassi Racing to bring home the trophy in July.”

Located in Montmeló, just outside Barcelona, Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya has been a fixture on the international motorsports stage since opening in 1991. The renowned road course has hosted some of the world’s most prestigious racing championships, including FIA Formula One and MotoGP, and is recognized for its combination of high-speed corners, technical sections and demanding layout.

The addition of Barcelona marks another significant milestone for INDYCAR as the series continues to introduce its high-speed, ultra-competitive brand of racing to new audiences and build upon its growing momentum.

"The arrival of INDYCAR is a major milestone and an exciting challenge for the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya,” Chairman of the Board of Fira de Barcelona and Fira Circuit Pau Relat said. “Bringing one of the most prestigious and spectacular championships in global motorsport to our venue strengthens our international positioning, connects us with new audiences and markets, and reinforces our strategy of diversifying the circuit’s activity through world-class events. We are working with a long-term vision to make INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona a benchmark event on the international racing calendar for years to come."

Phase Two of the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule, which will include a listing of all races in next year’s championship, will be announced shortly. Tune-in times for next season’s events will be announced at a later date.

title: Three-Day Tickets for St. Petersburg Go On Sale Friday, Oct. 23
excerpt:
Three-day tickets for the 2027 Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg go on sale to the public at 10 a.m. ET Friday, Oct. 23, giving fans the opportunity to secure their place at the 23rd running of the downtown tradition March 5-7, 2027.

Tickets will be available at gpstpete.com, with three-day reserved Grandstand seats starting at $150 and three-day General Admission tickets starting at $95. Junior pricing is available for fans ages 12 and under. Fans can also elevate their race weekend with Pit Passes, Firestone IndyCar Paddock Passes and Rookie Racers memberships for young motorsports enthusiasts ages 5-12. Single-day tickets will go on sale in the new year.

The 2027 event will mark the 17th time the Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg has opened the NTT INDYCAR SERIES season, placing this destination city at the center of the sport’s opening-weekend spotlight.

For tickets, event updates and additional information, visit gpstpete.com or follow the Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg on social media using #FirestoneGP.

The complete weekend racing and festival schedule will be announced at a later date.

title: 4 DAYS AGO •Track News Race On: A Look at Most Competitive Events of 2026 Season
excerpt:
In a season in which reigning NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou won six races, eight NTT P1 Awards and secured a record-tying fourth consecutive championship, it would seem it wasn’t the most competitive of seasons. Not so.

Yes, Palou put a number on his rivals in the overall standings, winning his fifth title in a six-year span by 86 points, but compelling races ran through the 18-race schedule.

Seven races saw a margin of victory of less than a second. One of those – the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge – was won by a driver who was in third place heading to the final lap. Felix Rosenqvist of Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian won the “500” in the most dramatic fashion ever, using a pass within yards of the checkered flag to record the closest 1-2 finish in event history (.0233 of a second over Team Penske’s David Malukas).

There were eight instances where this year’s race winner didn’t lead the most laps, and in the first 10 races the winner’s average starting position was 5.5. Arrow McLaren’s Christian Lundgaard had the season’s lowest starting position among the race winners: 12th in the XPEL Grand Prix at Road America.

A look at five of those competitive races in order of when they were staged:

Newgarden Surges Late to Win at Phoenix

Two-time series champion Josef Newgarden earned the 33rd victory of his career – the 19th on ovals – by chasing down and passing race leader Kyle Kirkwood with seven laps remaining in the Good Ranchers 250. Team Penske standout Newgarden, who started 11th, went on to win by 1.7937 seconds.

Although clearly a dominant oval racer, Newgarden (photo, above, front) led only eight of the 250 laps, benefiting from a set of new tires on the final pit stop. He said he was surprised to win the series’ first race at the track since 2018, a race he also won.

This race featured 565 on-track passes, an INDYCAR SERIES race at the 1-mile desert oval.

Andretti Global’s Will Power and Ed Carpenter Racing’s Christian Rasmussen looked like possible winners until their ferocious battle for the lead ended with the left front wing end plate of Rasmussen’s car making contact with the right rear tire of Power’s car. The impact in Turn 2 cut Power’s tire, triggering the final caution period as both cars were damaged.

Power had led 10 laps, Rasmussen 69. They were among the eight drivers who led as many laps (or more) than Newgarden. Malukas, who finished third, led a race-high 73 laps from the pole.

Rasmussen, who had made several daring passes, tried to hang on to the lead during the final restart, but his damaged car was no match for Andretti Global’s Kirkwood and, later, Newgarden. Rasmussen faded to 14th place.

Kirkwood Passes Palou To Win New Arlington Race

The first of three new street races during the season was fun on so many levels.

To begin with, the three-day spectator turnout was sensational, and the circuit delivered action aplenty.

Five drivers led the 70-lap main event, and how’s this for competitive balance: Three drivers led a race-high 16 laps, and another led 15 laps. Those drivers were Kirkwood, Palou and Power with 16 laps led, and pole winner Marcus Ericsson led 15 laps. They also were the top four finishers, respectively.

Rosenqvist also led the race for seven laps. All five of the leaders started in the top five except Kirkwood (photo, above), who was disappointed with his qualifying run and settled for the seventh starting position. His charge through the field was impressive.

Palou had the lead over Kirkwood when they each made their final pit stops on the preferred three-stop strategy on Lap 49. Palou’s crew got him away in 7.7 seconds while Kirkwood’s service was 9.5 seconds due to a slow change of the right rear wheel.

Palou exited with a 2.2-second lead, but Kirkwood used his speed to close, and he dove to the inside in Turn 13 near the end of Lap 55 and made the daring pass attempt stick.

Kirkwood pulled away to a 5.5-second lead, but that advantage evaporated when a caution came out on Lap 68. That set up a one-lap shootout, which Kirkwood mastered for his first of two victories on the season.

Rosenqvist Delivers All-Time Last Lap To Win Indy 500

Epic is the best word to describe the ending of this year’s “500” at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

Rosenqvist (photo, above) capped his magical May by edging Malukas in a last-lap drag race to the Yard of Bricks, but Malukas was not Rosenqvist’s only last-lap obstacle. First, he had to clear teammate Marcus Armstrong, who had the lead coming to the white flag and then after being passed by Malukas spent 20-plus seconds – and most of four corners – on the inside of Rosenqvist in a stirring side-by-side duel.

The Swede finally cleared Armstrong coming out of Turn 4, then darted into Malukas’ draft for a slingshot pass as the checkered flags awaited. The margin of victory was a scant .0233 of a second, breaking the record for the previous closest finish in event history: Al Unser Jr. held off a charging Scott Goodyear by .043 of a second in 1992.

Rosenqvist’s pass was one of an event-record 70 lead changes over 200 scintillating laps, breaking the previous mark of 68 set in 2013.

Armstrong’s lost momentum in the final charge dropped him to fifth place behind Team Penske’s Scott McLaughlin and Arrow McLaren’s Pato O’Ward in a three-wide finish. An incredible .4360 of a second separated the top five finishers.

Rosenqvist’s pass was one of 629 in the race, including 567 for position.

Lundgaard Recovers To Win at Road America

The XPEL Grand Prix at Road America was so competitive that three drivers led more laps than Lundgaard, who won the race.

The Arrow McLaren driver (photo, above, front) led the final four laps of the 55-lap contest to secure his third career series victory. But what made the win sweet was how far he came to achieve it.

Starting 12th, Lundgaard took contact on the opening lap, which knocked him to last place in the 25-car running order. He and his team used a combination of strategy, speed and a bit of good fortune to scramble all the way to the top spot.

The race proved to be another strong showing for Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian, which won the “500” with Rosenqvist and finished fifth with Armstrong. They combined to lead 18 and 14 laps, respectively, with Palou leading 13. Armstrong was poised to win his first series race – he led by nearly three seconds with five laps to go – before a mechanical failure cruelly robbed him of that. His stricken machine finally lost power in Turn 5 on Lap 53, triggering a caution period and a one-lap race to the checkered flag.

That final lap saw a tangle for third place between Power and Graham Rahal. The latter’s car got the worst of it, hitting the outside wall before sliding into Canada Corner’s gravel.

That was the climax to a thrilling race filled with varying tire strategies and fierce competition for nearly every position. But nothing was more exciting or improbable than Lundgaard’s charge to the front.

Ericsson’s Late Charge Takes New Markham Race

New street circuits come with questions about how well they’ll race. This first event answered them.

The Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham offered one of the best shows of the season, with five drivers exchanging the lead in the 90-lap affair. Three of those drivers led 20 or more laps each. Second-year driver Louis Foster of Rahal Letterman Lanigan led the first 32 laps from the pole, shuffled back to the 12th position due to pitting under the first caution.

Foster came charging back, advancing eight positions and stalking Ericsson for third place when they approached Turn 3 on Lap 43. Foster went to the inside of Ericsson but clipped the left-side wall, contact which shot him straight into the concrete barrier on the right. The impact was virtually head-on, a major shunt. That spot in the track similarly claimed Kirkwood, who was running third behind his two teammates (Power and Ericsson). His impact was just as fierce.

The second half of the race featured a showdown between Dale Coyne Racing’s Romain Grosjean, who led 28 laps, and Ericsson (photo, top). For a time, it appeared Grosjean was poised for his first series victory as Ericsson had pitted for new tires.

With Ericsson just 10 days from being confirmed to return to Andretti Global for a fourth season, the drama was rich. Ericsson’s pit stop had dropped him to seventh place, but his speed was undeniable. He caught and passed Grosjean five laps from the finish to send him on his way to his first series win 63 races dating back to his 2023 season-opening victory in St. Petersburg.

The margin of victory was a deceiving 7.5305 seconds.

title: Inside Line: ‘I Didn’t See That Coming’
excerpt:
Today’s question: What is your “I didn’t see that coming” moment of the 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season?

Curt Cavin: There are many moments from the past season to choose from, but I’m still dazzled by Kyle Kirkwood’s surprising pass of Alex Palou late in the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington (photo, above). The two series stars were locked in a fierce battle for the lead, and Kirkwood appeared to have the faster car. Still, Kirkwood had to pass the four-time series champion, and he opted for the opportunity in a corner that few thought would be available to him. Kirkwood dove to the inside of Palou approaching Turn 14, drawing high-pitched reactions from all three FOX broadcasters. Townsend Bell called it “a Hail Mary in the shadows of (the Cowboys’) stadium.” James Hinchcliffe wondered if Kirkwood surprised even himself when he braked late and drew alongside Palou with corner fast approaching. Felix Rosenqvist had the pass of the season to win the Indianapolis 500, but in my opinion this pass was No. 2 on the year’s list.

Eric Smith: This is a great question, and it’s hard to narrow it down to just one. I went outside the box with my “I didn’t see that coming.” Mine is Will Power AND Scott Dixon going winless and finishing outside the top 10 in the championship standings. Power (photo, above, right) had finished in the top 10 in every full-time season since 2009. Granted, this was his first year with Andretti Global after 17 seasons with Team Penske, but seeing him go winless while his teammates combined for three wins was shocking. The same goes for Dixon. His streak of 21 consecutive seasons with at least one victory came to an end, as did his run of 20 straight years finishing in the top six in the championship standings. He wound up 12th. There are plenty of individual race moments you could make a case for, but my pick is seeing two drivers with eight combined series championships -- and the only drivers other than Alex Palou to win a title since 2020 – not be in the top 10 of the championship race.

Arni Sribhen: Legendary baseball broadcaster Jack Buck delivered the iconic call, “I don’t believe what I just saw!” after seeing Kirk Gibson’s game-winning, pinch-hit home run in the 1988 World Series. I had the same thought when I saw this year’s Indianapolis 500 finish. Sure, we’ve seen last-lap Indy 500 duels before (I mean, I watch a 1992 finish video set to the radio call every May), but Felix Rosenqvist’s final Brickyard circuit will be one we’ll talk about for years to come. Rosenqvist drew alongside Meyer Shank Racing teammate Marcus Armstrong as they crossed the historic Yard of Bricks. The No. 60 car spent most of the lap on the outside of Armstrong before finally clearing him in the middle of Turn 4. From there, Rosenqvist’s car seemed to hit the video game-like boost button as he quickly closed on race leader David Malukas, sweeping past him just ahead of the checkered flag. The gap was a scant .0233 of a second (photo, above). A wow moment indeed.

Paul Kelly: This was a tough question that came down to two possible answers for me: The Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. or Scott Dixon’s move from Chip Ganassi Racing to Arrow McLaren. But I must choose the race in the capital (photo, top). I remember hearing rumblings about this once-in-a-lifetime event in early January, right after returning from the holidays, but dismissed the idea almost immediately. A race in D.C.? With less than a year to pull it off? No way. But the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. was announced Jan. 30 and built and executed in less than seven months by Bud Denker and his Penske Entertainment and local D.C. team. It was a spectacular setting for a race with all sorts of logistical and organizational hurdles, and INDYCAR had the audacity to agree to stage the event and then pulled it off with such success. I would have thought a year ago that I had a better chance of making the NHL as a 60-year-old than a race taking place around the National Mall and the U.S. Capitol. Well, after INDYCAR pulled this off as a spectacular success, maybe I should sharpen my skates and tape my stick.

title: Who Will Be INDYCAR SERIES’ 300th Driver To Enter Victory Lane?
excerpt:
The race to No. 300 is on.

That statistical footnote in NTT INDYCAR SERIES history might not mean something to everyone, but it will be significant to someone when it happens. So, what does 300 represent? The number of drivers to have won races in this series.

Major U.S. open-wheel racing traces its roots to 1909, and the first recorded event consisted of three separate road races Saturday, June 12 in Portland, Oregon. Howard Covey won that first contest in a Cadillac, making him the first race winner in this sport’s history.

Interestingly, that’s the only race Covey ever won, and that race spanned only three laps. He averaged less than 56 mph.

In the years since, drivers from many corners of the globe have won races. Some have become legends. Names like Ray Harroun, Ralph DePalma, Earl Cooper and Tommy Milton in the earliest years followed by Louis Meyer, Mauri Rose, Wilbur Shaw, Rex Mays and Ted Horn. In the roadster heyday, the winners were the likes of Jimmy Bryan, Tony Bettenhausen, Rodger Ward, A.J. Foyt and Parnelli Jones.

Following the Andrettis, Unsers, Johnny Rutherford, Gordon Johncock, Rick Mears and Tom Sneva were the household names became Bobby Rahal, Emerson Fittipaldi, Arie Luyendyk, Nigel Mansell and others. In the 2000s, Juan Pablo Montoya, Gil de Ferran, Sam Hornish Jr., Paul Tracy, Sebastien Bourdais, Tony Kanaan, Dan Wheldon and Dario Franchitti reigned.

The 2026 cast featured Scott Dixon, Helio Castroneves, Will Power, Josef Newgarden, Alex Palou and more. Eighteen of the 33 drivers who suited up this year are among the first 299 drivers to win a race in this series. The most recent of those was Christian Rasmussen in 2025 at Milwaukee.

Someone will be next.

David Malukas (photo, top) figures to be the best bet. His five seasons in the series have produced six runner-up finishes, including the past two years of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. Continuing to drive for the winningest team in the sport’s history – Team Penske – should keep him challenging for victories on any type of circuit.

Malukas had four second-place and two third-place finishes this year, and he finished second in laps led with 282 laps.

Kyffin Simpson also drives for one of the sport’s elite organizations, which makes him one to watch. Simpson (photo, above) doesn’t have Malukas’ record over his three seasons, but as a Chip Ganassi Racing driver he will have five-time and reigning series champion Alex Palou and Christian Lundgaard, a three-time race winner, to draw insight from next season. Malukas and Simpson were the top two non-winners in this year’s standings.

One of the more surprising moments of this year’s 18-race schedule was Marcus Armstrong leading the “500” coming to the white flag. He put up a stellar fight with fellow Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian teammate Felix Rosenqvist over most of the final lap before seeing the eventual race winner scoot past in Turn 4. Armstrong (photo, above) then lost a three-way battle for third place with Team Penske’s Scott McLaughlin and Arrow McLaren’s Pato O’Ward. Those two drivers have combined for 20 series victories.

Armstrong was poised to win this year’s XPEL Grand Prix at Road America before a mechanical failure dropped him from the lead five laps from the finish. Next year, Armstrong will have Mick Schumacher, the son of seven-time Formula One champion Michael Schumacher, as a teammate, and Schumacher’s second INDYCAR SERIES season figures to be stronger than his rookie campaign.

Louis Foster (photo, above) of Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing is another driver who nearly broke through in 2026. In the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham, he won his second career NTT P1 Award, led the first 32 laps of the race before getting shuffled back during the first pit stop and was fourth when he hit the barrier to end his race.

Romain Grosjean nearly went on to earn his first series victory that day at Markham. He led 28 laps in the second half of the race for Dale Coyne Racing before settling for his sixth career second-place finish (Andretti Global’s Marcus Ericsson overtook him with five laps remaining). Grosjean has not been confirmed to a seat for next season.

Conor Daly also has been on the verge of winning. He has two career podium finishes, the most recent in 2024 at Milwaukee Mile. Daly will be full-time in 2027 with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing’s new full-season Honda entry.

The 2027 season begins Sunday, March 7 with the Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg. All of next year’s races are scheduled to air live on FOX.

title: Notebook: Team Penske, Hitachi Extend Partnership
excerpt:
Team Penske and Hitachi, Ltd. announced Oct. 20 an extension to their NTT INDYCAR SERIES sponsorship agreement. Hitachi will maintain its branding on the front wings of Team Penske’s No. 2, No. 3 and No. 12 Chevrolet-powered entries for the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season.

The sponsorship, which began in 2012, is a cornerstone of Hitachi and Team Penske’s multifaceted partnership. Hitachi continues to serve as an important technology partner to Penske, spanning application development, digital engineering, cybersecurity, data and AI, and managed services since 2018.

“We are proud of the strong partnership we have built with Penske Group over the past 14 years,” said Charlie Takeuchi, president and CEO of Hitachi Americas. “From the excitement of our partnership with Team Penske on the track to the work we do alongside Penske’s businesses using AI and digital engineering, we look forward to continuing our partnership and building what’s next together.”

Hitachi and Penske have also co-created innovative technologies to transform Penske's fleet maintenance operations, driving more than $18 million in annualized savings through faster diagnostics and predictive maintenance, and helping prevent over 90,000 breakdowns.

“Hitachi is a trusted global brand and a critical partner across the Penske organization,” said Jonathan Diuguid, Team Penske president, INDYCAR. “Our relationship continues to pay dividends on and off the track, and we’re glad to continue that momentum as we mark Team Penske’s 60th anniversary.”

Rasmussen Set for Turkey Night Midget Debut

Christian Rasmussen will trade his No. 21 ECR Chevrolet for a dirt midget over Thanksgiving weekend, making his debut in the 85th Annual ARP Turkey Night Grand Prix on Saturday, Nov. 28 at Ventura Raceway in Southern California.

Rasmussen (photo, above) will drive a Spike chassis fielded by car owner Johnny Cofer, the father of Rasmussen’s girlfriend, former USAC Midget driver Maria Cofer. The entry also has support from the Agajanian family and will feature a tribute to the iconic 1952 Agajanian Special, which Troy Ruttman drove to victory in the Indianapolis 500.

The 98-lap Turkey Night Grand Prix serves as the season finale of the USAC National Midget Championship. A holiday racing tradition dating to 1934, the event is considered the third-longest-running race in the United States, behind the Indianapolis 500 and the Pikes Peak International Hill Climb.

Rasmussen returns to ECR for the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season, his third full-time campaign with the team after also competing part time for ECR in 2024. He earned his first career INDYCAR SERIES victory Aug. 24, 2025, at the Milwaukee Mile.

The Dane also has championship credentials throughout the junior categories, winning the USF2000 title in 2020, Indy Pro 2000 in 2021 and INDY NXT by Firestone in 2023. He became the second driver to win championships at every level of the ladder leading to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

title: Pato O’Ward Ready To Take Final Step Among Series Elite in 2027
excerpt:
Pato O’Ward has accomplished almost everything a driver can ask for in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

He has 12 career victories. He has finished among the top five in the championship six times in his seven full-time seasons. He finished a career-best second in the standings in 2025 and has been runner-up twice in the Indianapolis 500.

But two accomplishments continue to elude the popular Mexican driver: an Indianapolis 500 victory and an NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship. He’s getting closer to both.

O’Ward finished fourth in the 2026 championship, adding three victories, 10 top-five finishes and 11 top-10 results to his résumé. He closed the season especially strong, sweeping both races at Milwaukee Mile and scoring three top-five finishes in the final five events. Yet O’Ward’s season wasn’t always as straightforward as those numbers suggest.

“It was a bit of an odd one,” he said. “I felt very confused. I’m always kind of on my own island, always have been, and this year I just couldn’t seem to get a direction. More times than not, I’m more kind of like, ‘Where do we go?’ It was one of those seasons.”

Arrow McLaren still produced an impressive season, with Christian Lundgaard third in the standings and O’Ward fourth. Only Alex Palou of Chip Ganassi Racing and Kyle Kirkwood of Andretti Global finished ahead of the Arrow McLaren duo.

O’Ward and the team are digging deep in data this offseason to figure out how to improve. They’re close. It’s just how many of those top-five finishes could have landed on the podium. The team is all-in on helping O’Ward, so much so it’s surrounded him with three Indy 500-winning teammates and seven combined championships.

The team didn’t retain Lundgaard or Nolan Siegel, O’Ward’s teammates the past two seasons. Lundgaard finished in the top five in points in each of the last two seasons and won two races this past season. Arrow McLaren brought back Felix Rosenqvist and added six-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Scott Dixon as replacements. (Photo above, from left: O’Ward, Rosenqvist, Dixon)

Rosenqvist returns following a three-year stint with Arrow McLaren from 2021-23. He and O’Ward became close friends during that time and have remained close. Rosenqvist drove for Meyer Shank Racing the past three seasons and won the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.

Dixon brings a résumé no current driver in the series can match. The 2008 Indianapolis 500 winner has 59 career INDYCAR SERIES victories and six championships. Ryan Hunter-Reay returns to the team for a second consecutive year as an Indy 500-only participant. Hunter-Reay won the 2012 championship and 2014 Indianapolis 500.

That gives O’Ward three highly accomplished teammates from whom he can learn as he continues his pursuit of the two biggest goals missing from his résumé. It’s a combination that gives Arrow McLaren optimism entering 2027, especially after team principal Tony Kanaan called 2026 the best season in team history.

“There is so much to be proud of this past season, starting with our move into our new home, the McLaren Racing Center, in Indianapolis where we launched our season liveries back in February,” Kanaan said. “We celebrated Christian’s (Lundgaard) first Arrow McLaren win at the Indy GP; we sped down the Miami streets to unveil Ryan Hunter-Reay’s Indy 500 livery; we snagged our team’s first-ever 1-2 finish at Mid-Ohio; we raced in awesome new markets (Phoenix, Arlington, Markham and Washington); and we made history in Milwaukee with Pato’s back-to-back wins in a single day, just to name a few of the highs through the year.”

Kanaan isn’t satisfied with simply celebrating what Arrow McLaren accomplished in 2026. He views the season as a foundation for something bigger, with O’Ward at the center of those plans.

“We’ve been fighting to establish our team among the top in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, and we proved ourselves this year, but that doesn’t mean we’re ready to settle,” Kanaan said. “Just the opposite. I’ve always said winning is addicting. We’re still building, still developing and still racing for more wins.

“We’re building on a strong foundation. The experience Pato, Scott and Felix bring is nearly unmatched, and we’re working hard this offseason to hit the ground running in St. Pete next March.

“And of course, we’re locked in on the Indy 500. We’re hyper-focused on making a statement at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, one that ends with milk.”

The challenge for O’Ward is turning consistency, speed and experience into the two achievements that have remained just out of reach. His 2026 season showed he can contend throughout a championship battle. His late-season surge provided momentum. It’s time to capitalize.

“It’s all about building on what you learned the previous year,” O’Ward said. “Doesn’t always work out perfect, but I’ve got some very experienced teammates coming into the picture, and I’m so excited to learn from them.”

title: Domination Station: Five Most Punishing Performances of 2026
excerpt:
Even with Alex Palou winning five NTT INDYCAR SERIES championships in the past six years, this field remains the most competitive group in motorsports.

Yet, there were race weekends where drivers and their teams dominated. Often, that was Palou and Chip Ganassi Racing, but not always.

Arrow McLaren had some of those events. Andretti Global and Team Penske did, as well.

Obviously, Palou had the most convincing victories, and stacking them together helped mount an 86-point advantage at season’s end. His drives in the Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg (led 59 of the 100 laps and finished 12.4948 seconds ahead of Team Penske’s Scott McLaughlin) merited consideration for one of the best five of the season, as well as his winning effort from the pole in the Chevrolet Grand Prix of Detroit (71 of 100 laps led).

Palou also had a streak of five consecutive poles from the Sonsio Grand Prix at Indianapolis Motor Speedway through the XPEL Grand Prix at Road America, and that run of speed in qualifying was demoralizing to several of his challengers.

But Palou wasn’t the only driver who had a convincing weekend. One that didn’t make the season’s top five was Marcus Ericsson’s winning run for Andretti Global in the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham, a 7.5305-second finish ahead of Dale Coyne Racing’s Romain Grosjean on the new street circuit.

Only one performance on an oval track made the top five – more on that below – but it’s worth noting that Team Penske’s Josef Newgarden continued his prowess on shorter tracks, winning both the Good Ranchers 250 at Phoenix Raceway and the Bommarito Automotive Group 500 at World Wide Technology Raceway. Newgarden now has 20 oval victories in his INDYCAR SERIES career.

The top five most dominating performances in order of when they occurred during the year:

Alex Palou, Children’s of Alabama Indy Grand Prix

This drive at Barber Motorsports Park was arguably the best of Palou’s efforts in a six-win season that resulted in a fifth championship. He won the NTT P1 Award for the first of what would be eight times during the year, and he effectively led the race wire to wire.

Palou kept the lead at the green flag, leading the first 43 laps before pitting. He then relinquished the lead a second time on Lap 65 when he scooted to pit road for fuel and tires, and in each instance, he only dropped to third place before quickly cycling back to the front as others pitted.

Palou led 79 of the 90 laps (87.8 percent).

Palou’s margin of victory over Arrow McLaren’s Christian Lundgaard was a season-high 13.2775 seconds. Palou’s advantage at the end of the St. Petersburg race was the second-largest margin of the season.

Arrow McLaren, The Honda Indy 200 at Mid-Ohio

Pato O’Ward and Lundgaard combined to lead 86 of the 90 laps (95.6 percent) at the Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course, the most significant beatdown by a single team during the season.

Lundgaard, who edged O’Ward for the pole, led the first 41 laps before O’Ward snuck past through a thrilling side-by-side battle set up by Lundgaard drifting wide in Turn 2. O’Ward effectively led the rest of the way, relinquishing the top spot briefly to pit.

Newgarden led Laps 49 and 50 while Andretti Global’s Will Power held the top spot on Laps 66 and 67.

The 1-2 finish was the first for Arrow McLaren in this series, and it was the first win for O’Ward in nearly a year since he won the 2025 street race in Toronto.

Kyle Kirkwood, Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C.

Kirkwood delivered a masterful performance in the massively important new street race in the nation’s capital.

The Andretti Global driver qualified second behind Palou but jumped the reigning series champion on the opening lap en route to leading 128 of the 147 laps (87.1 percent).

Kirkwood’s domination was aided by the struggles of Palou and the accident of McLaughlin. While trying to hold the lead, McLaughlin hit the Turn 1 tire barrier on the restart at Lap 129.

Kirkwood’s margin of victory over Lundgaard was 3.0906 seconds. Kirkwood also won another of the season’s first-year street races, the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington, although his lead at the finish of that race was only .3140 of a second over Palou.

Pato O’Ward, Snap-On INDYCAR Weekend

O’Ward won his second and third races of the season on the same Wisconsin day.

The Arrow McLaren driver combined to lead 174 of the 500 laps in the doubleheader (34.8 percent). His two margins of victory were .7916 of a second (over McLaughlin) and 1.7535 seconds (over Team Penske’s David Malukas).

The two wins gave three for his career at the historic Milwaukee Mile.

The last driver to sweep a doubleheader was Newgarden at Iowa Speedway in 2023.

Scott McLaughlin, Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey

McLaughlin saved his best for the last race of the season, and the virtual wire-to-wire victory at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca earned him his first victory in more than two years. His drought had been 36 races.

McLaughlin led a season-high 87 of the 95 laps from the pole (91.6 percent), although his margin of victory over Kirkwood didn’t necessarily reflect that dominance. It was only 1.3739 seconds.

title: Get Your Tickets: Arlington On Sale Now, Long Beach Available Sunday
excerpt:
Single-day ticket options for the 2027 Java House Grand Prix of Arlington are on sale now at gparlington.com.

The Java House Grand Prix of Arlington (photo, top) returns Friday, March 19 through Sunday, March 21 to the streets of Arlington, Texas, following a record-breaking inaugural event that welcomed tens of thousands of fans to Arlington’s Entertainment District. The stars of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES are back in North Texas for a weekend of world-class racing and entertainment.

Three-day ticket packages, paddock passes and parking also remain available while supplies last.

The Java House Grand Prix of Arlington features a 2.73-mile temporary street circuit woven throughout Arlington's Entertainment District. The challenging, 14-turn course provides fans with a unique opportunity to experience the speed, sound and excitement of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in one of the country's premier sports and entertainment destinations.

Fans can get even closer to the action with the purchase of a paddock pass, for exclusive garage access where INDYCAR teams work on their race cars all weekend long. The event also features a variety of premium viewing experiences, including reserved grandstand seating and the WinStar Winners Club.

The WinStar Winners Club delivers an unparalleled Race Day experience, featuring tiered seating, high-top tables and bar rails with exceptional views of pit lane, the front straightaway and Turn 1. A portion of the club extends directly over the racetrack, offering guests the thrilling perspective of “The Fastest Racing on Earth” directly beneath them.

Adding to the exclusivity, the winner's podium is integrated into the WinStar Winners Club, providing guests with an up-close view of the victory celebrations following every race throughout the weekend – an experience unique to the INDYCAR schedule. All-inclusive amenities include food, beer, wine, spirits, soft drinks, water, paddock access and parking.

Single day practice tickets start at $20, and Race Day tickets start at $100. Fans can get 3-day tickets starting at $150. Children under 12 are admitted free in general admission areas at the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington when accompanied by an adult general admission ticketholder.

Long Beach Tickets Go On Sale Sunday, Oct. 18

Tickets go on sale at 1 p.m. ET Sunday, Oct. 18 for the 2027 Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach, the longest-running street race on the NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule. The annual festival of speed in Southern California (photo, above) takes place Friday, April 16 through Sunday, April 18 on the iconic 11-turn, 1.968-mile street circuit.

Starting at 1 p.m. ET Sunday, fans can select and pay for their 2027 Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach seats, parking and paddock passes online at gplb.com. Ticket orders can also be placed by calling the toll-free ticket hotline, (888) 827-7333.

Off the track and free to all race attendees will be the popular Lifestyle Expo featuring more than 100 exhibitors showcasing the latest in automotive, travel, home, sustainability, fitness and recreation as well as the large Family Fun Zone in the Long Beach Arena. There will also be Friday and Saturday evening concerts, more than 150 concession stands throughout the venue, unique car displays, driver autograph sessions, the CARnival car show and a wide variety of activities for everyone.

Ticket prices range from $59 for a Friday General Admission ticket to $232 for a three-day ticket that includes Saturday/Sunday reserved seating in grandstand upper levels. Prepaid parking packages are also available, along with ADA seating, NTT INDYCAR SERIES paddock passes, Super Photo tickets and a wide variety of hospitality packages. Children 12 years and under will be admitted free with a ticketed adult, although they will need a Junior ticket to sit in the grandstands.

title: Alex Palou To Rev Up Indiana Football Fans Before Buckeye Showdown
excerpt:
Alex Palou has a new role for Saturday’s college football showdown between Indiana University and Ohio State on FOX. He’s the honorary driver of an Indiana University-themed NTT INDYCAR SERIES race car.

Palou was named Thursday to fill in for Hoosier the Bison, IU’s mascot, who has driven the car while leading the Hoosiers out of the tunnel before each home game at Memorial Stadium this season.

The five-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion, a native of Spain, has become an avid Indiana University sports fan since making Indianapolis his home. He also has visited IU’s Bloomington campus several times ahead of big games as part of FOX Sports’ promotional activities.

“I’m following IU now,” Palou said during FOX Sports’ “Big Noon Kickoff” before a game last year. “It’s (IU atmosphere) a little more rowdy than I thought. I love it.”

Palou’s honorary role is the latest stop in a busy stretch behind the wheel of a variety of race cars -- none of them his No. 10 Chip Ganassi Racing Honda.

On Oct. 3, he competed in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship’s Petit Le Mans for Meyer Shank Racing. He then drove the No. 80 Lone Star Racing Mercedes-AMG in last weekend’s Intercontinental GT Challenge Indianapolis 8 Hour during practice and qualifying but never turned a wheel in the race due to being taken out in an accident before his first stint. On Monday, Palou tested the IR-28, the new NTT INDYCAR SERIES chassis scheduled to debut in 2028, at Sebring International Raceway.

Friday, Palou will drive INDY NXT by Firestone machinery for the first time, participating in the Chris Griffis Memorial Test on the 2.439-mile, 14-turn Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course. He is filling in for Chip Ganassi Racing’s full-time INDY NXT driver Carson Etter, who underwent offseason shoulder surgery.

Saturday’s game adds another dimension to Palou’s growing connection with IU. FOX Sports, which became the exclusive television provider of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES ahead of the 2025 season, will broadcast the Ohio State-Indiana matchup.

Palou, the 2025 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner, enters Saturday’s game following a championship season in which he captured his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES title. His fourth consecutive championship in 2026 tied him with Sébastien Bourdais, who won four straight titles from 2004-07. No driver has won five consecutive championships. Only A.J. Foyt, with seven titles, and Scott Dixon, with six, have won more career championships than Palou.

title: Inside Line: Next First-Time Series Champion?
excerpt:
Today’s question: Who will be the next first-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion?

Curt Cavin: Pato O’Ward and Kyle Kirkwood are the past two series runners-up, but I believe Kirkwood (photo, top) is the more likely of the two to climb a higher step, especially as you review his progression since joining the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in 2022. He finished 24th (with AJ Foyt Racing) and then 11th, seventh, fourth and second in four seasons with Andretti Global. I don’t think Kirkwood wins next year’s championship, and he might have to wait a couple of years for Alex Palou to get bored, but I think he will soon earn his way into the champion’s room as his team’s first such winner since Ryan Hunter-Reay in 2012. (By the way, there will soon be significant chatter about Kirkwood being the series’ next big free agent, but I think he remains loyal to Andretti Global and drives the No. 27 Honda for years to come.)

Eric Smith: I believe Scott McLaughlin will be the next first-time champion. If anyone is going to knock Alex Palou off his perch, I don’t see it being a teammate. Scott Dixon couldn’t do it over the past four years, and now he’s moving to Arrow McLaren. If Palou is topped, I sense a down year for the entire Chip Ganassi Racing organization. So why not look to Team Penske, a team with 17 series titles, just one behind Ganassi’s 18? McLaughlin (photo, above) closed out 2026 in strong fashion, posting three consecutive top-five finishes, including a season-finale victory at Laguna Seca. He also knows what it takes to win a championship, having claimed three Australian V8 Supercars titles. McLaughlin is a versatile driver who excels across all disciplines, and his time is coming. I believe he’ll win an INDYCAR SERIES championship within the next two to three years.

Arni Sribhen: The last 14 NTT INDYCAR SERIES champions have raced for either Chip Ganassi Racing or Team Penske, so the odds are high that the next first-time champion is already racing for one of those two teams. In fact, I think David Malukas has the best shot at winning an Astor Challenge Cup among the drivers who haven’t already won one. The evidence is there. Malukas (photo, above) had a breakout first season with Team Penske, though he didn’t reach victory lane. His four runner-up finishes show he’s knocking on the door of that first win, and when that happens, the wins may come in bunches. It’s reminiscent of Simon Pagenaud’s first few seasons with Penske. He was winless in his first season, then won the series championship the next season and was a contender for the next few seasons. I think Malukas may be on that same Penske path.

Paul Kelly: Christian Lundgaard. The Dane (photo, above) earned his first victory in 2023 from the pole on the streets of Toronto, with Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing. Then he added two road-course wins in 2026, at the Sonsio Grand Prix and Road America, with Arrow McLaren. The only missing link to becoming a champion is oval performance, and I think Lundgaard’s shortcomings on circle tracks are dwindling, as evidenced by his third- and sixth-place finishes in August at Milwaukee, the last oval event of the season. That acumen only will increase in Lundgaard’s move to Chip Ganassi Racing, where he will learn the fine art of oval racing from strategist Mike Hull and advisor Dario Franchitti, who also took awhile to figure out circle tracks before flourishing on them. And don’t forget that five-time series champion Alex Palou didn’t earn his first oval win until the 2025 Indianapolis 500, in his sixth season in the series. Finally, Arrow McLaren dumped Lundgaard for what it saw as his weakness on ovals. That stings. So, that rebuke will provide him with any extra motivation he needs. Beating Palou won’t be easy in ANY year, but Lundgaard is best positioned to do it.

title: Alex Palou To Help Ganassi Hone INDY NXT Setups at Griffis Test
excerpt:
Track News

Alex Palou has driven plenty of cars around Indianapolis Motor Speedway. This week, he’ll add another to the list.

Five-time and reigning NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Palou (photo, top) will drive the No. 11 Chip Ganassi Racing entry in the annual Chris Griffis Memorial Test on Friday, Oct. 16, on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course. Palou is filling in for CGR full-time INDY NXT driver Carson Etter, who is recovering from offseason shoulder surgery.

SEE: Griffis Test Entry List

The test honors Chris Griffis, the team manager for Schmidt Peterson Motorsports who died suddenly in September 2011. Friday’s session allows teams an opportunity to evaluate drivers and experiment with setups to begin preparations for the following season.

Palou is among 22 drivers scheduled to participate in the test, which runs from 9:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. ET. The Turn 2 spectator mounds will be open to fans.

Palou’s participation puts him in a rare position. He’s the four-time defending NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion stepping into the sport’s top developmental series after establishing himself at its highest level. Palou has never driven INDY NXT machinery. He joined the INDYCAR SERIES in 2020 with Dale Coyne Racing after building his career in European and Japanese series.

An INDY NXT car produces approximately 200-300 less horsepower and less downforce than an INDYCAR SERIES machine, along with different braking characteristics.

“It’ll be tough,” Palou said. “It’s very tough always to go from a car that has more downforce and carbon brakes and stuff to some car that is a bit smaller, less downforce, less power, and it doesn’t have as much performance. I’m excited to help the team see how that car feels.”

Palou believes familiarity with the 14-turn, 2.439-mile circuit helps the learning curve while testing the team's No. 11 INDY NXT car (photo, above). He’s a three-time Sonsio Grand Prix winner, each coming in the past four years.

“I’m excited to see what that car is capable of and helping the team as much as I can,” Palou said. “Its (the car) is probably like the current F3, which I drove almost eight to 10 years ago.

“So, yeah, it’ll take me a little bit to get used to. I know I won’t be at 100%. But I don’t think we don’t need to. The good thing is we’re not racing. We’re just testing. We’re just trying to learn as much as we can.”

Palou has been behind the wheel of many race cars lately. He drove an Acura prototype in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship race Oct. 3 at Petit Le Mans for Meyer Shank Racing. Palou then practiced and qualified the No. 80 Lone Star Racing Mercedes-AMG in last weekend’s Intercontinental GT Challenge Indianapolis 8 Hour on this same track, but he never turned a racing lap due to an early accident by one of his teammates. On Monday, he tested the IR-28, the new INDYCAR SERIES chassis scheduled to debut in 2028, at Sebring International Raceway.

He’s aware this test represents an opportunity for Chip Ganassi Racing to pursue a milestone that has eluded one of motorsports’ most successful organizations. CGR has amassed 25 championships across racing disciplines, including a record 18th INDYCAR SERIES title in 2026. The team has earned more than 275 victories in motorsports, including six Indianapolis 500 wins, eight Rolex 24 At Daytona victories and six wins apiece in the 12 Hours of Sebring and 24 Hours of Le Mans. But an INDY NXT race victory remains missing from its résumé.

Ganassi aims to change that by bringing Palou in for the day as the team works to find speed and strengthen its program.

The team will also field the No. 10 entry for Alessandro de Tullio, who competed as a rookie with AJ Foyt Racing this past season. De Tullio finished sixth in the championship standings with two victories. His eight pole positions fell one short of Pato O’Ward’s single-season series record set in 2018. Alexander Koreiba and Frankie Mossman join the duo for Friday’s test with CGR.
